Subject: Decentralized Pod Launch: comms draft + OKR alignment (Q2 prep)

Team —

Following up on the leadership offsite: attached is a first-pass comms draft for the decentralized pod pilot (see attachment: pod-launch-comms-draft.docx) and a proposed set of OKRs for Q2 that align with the initiative (pod-okrs-2028-q2.xlsx). High-level ask: please review and respond with final edits or blockers by EOD Friday so we can lock messaging for the 3/22 all-hands and QBR readout.

Why this matters: centralized release cadence has been a bottleneck for smaller feature work (model rollouts, infra tweaks). Pods are intended to reduce handoffs — pairing product, infra, and SRE for horizontal domains — to deliver multiple smaller model variants faster while preserving platform-level guardrails.

Key points in the draft:
- Pilot scope: 3 pods (Recommendations, Retrieval, Runtime Performance) for 12 weeks starting April 2
- Success metrics: median rollout lead time, number of rollouts without rollback, customer-perceived latency delta
- Org impact: a small number of role reassignments (rotational leads) and two new senior IC hires to staff pods

Open questions I want input on:
1) Are the proposed KR thresholds (50% faster lead time, <=1 rollback per pod) realistic?
2) Any expected compliance or audits concerns (Neha — flagged) around data access under pod boundaries?
3) Tone — is this too prescriptive for an initial pilot?

I copied Ellen from OrgDesign and People Strategy; they will help with change comms and role transitions.

Thanks — I put suggested edits in the Google doc link as well.

—Michael
Michael Grant
VP, Platform
Redwood Inference

Thanks Michael — good start. A few quick notes inline and summary here: 

- Scope: I agree with the three pilot pods but propose swapping Runtime Performance for 'Inference Ops' (combines serving + observability) — faster path to measurable latency improvements.
- KRs: 50% faster rollout lead time sounds aggressive for the first 12 weeks; suggest 30% as the pilot target and add a stretch KR at 50%.
- Staffing: recommend naming rotational leads now (I propose myself for Recommendations pod, Jonas to lead Inference Ops, and Neha to shadow for Retrieval) — that will help People Strategy plan transitions.
- Comms tone: make the first announcement more explicit about this being an experiment and include a feedback channel (Slack #pod-pilot-feedback) and weekly sync cadence.

I left inline comments on the Google doc and updated the OKR spreadsheet with the 30% baseline. Happy to sync 20 minutes after this thread if helpful.

—Marissa

Head of Product, Serving

I can host a 30-minute tech design review next Wednesday to surface integration gaps.

Thanks — quick read from security/compliance: 

- Pod-local experiments are ok under our current controls if they use centralized logging and RBAC; however, we must ensure KMS keys remain centralized and that any tenant data access is limited by policy.
- For the pilot, require two items before we go live: (1) data access checklist signed by pod leads, (2) audit hook enabled for model rollout events (we can do sampling to reduce volume).
- This adds ~1 week of gating for any pod that needs expanded dataset access; include that in your go/no-go evaluation.

I'm happy to coordinate the checklist with People Strategy and Ellen.

—Neha

Nice work on the draft. A couple of executive points before we send broadly: 

1) Positioning: Lead with the customer impact (faster model iterations, lower latency for pilot customers) and emphasize that this is a tightly scoped experiment with explicit rollback paths.
2) Org changes: call out rotational nature of leads and date-bound expectations to reduce anxiety. People Strategy should include FAQ for managers.
3) QBR: include a one-slide readout with success metrics and risks; copy the JIRA ticket for the QBR deck.

Approve sending the internal announcement to managers and pod participants next Monday, with a follow-up all-hands mention on 3/22. Ellen & People Strategy — pls confirm you can support manager FAQs and role transition comms.

Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference
